text:
maya: Quick notice: PR-15001 needs 2 approvals + a rebase before maintenance freeze at 21:00 UTC. CI is flaky on integration-test-session. If we don't have approvals + green by 20:30 UTC, we should either queue for after the freeze or land with a tight canary + rollback. Any blockers?
sam: I can do a review now, should finish by 20:15 UTC.
andre: Does this include any migration scripts? we can't land mid-window if so.
maya: No DB migrations, just request routing + feature flag `enable_new_route`. Theres a merge conflict in tests/test_routing.py that needs a small rebase.
jen: Noted. I'm watching the flaky macOS integration-test-session failure  I can try a rerun if someone requeues.
ci-bot: CI started for PR-15001: https://ci.redwood.example/15001  running integration-test-session
deploy-bot: Heads-up: maintenance freeze 21:00-22:00 UTC  merges blocked unless pre-approved and green.
sam: If we need a rebase slot, when's the latest window?
maya: There's a 10-min rebase window at 20:20-20:30 UTC on the release calendar. Please rebase with:
```
git checkout pr-15001
git pull --rebase origin/main
git push -f origin pr-15001
```
I'll be ready to merge if approvals + CI pass.
andre: I can review after 20:10 UTC. If tests pass and I approve, who will merge?
jen: I can be merge watcher and run the canary. Plan: 3% canary at landing, monitor 15m, rollback immediately on errors >0.5% or latency +20%. I'll add a temporary alert.
maya: Approvals requested from @sam and @andre  pushed a tiny fix for a flaky assert.
sam: LGTM :thumbsup: approved.
andre: Approved, left one suggestion but not blocking.
ci-bot: CI pipeline passed: integration-test-session  all checks green for PR-15001.
deploy-bot: Manual canary scheduled: PR-15001 -> canary 3% at 20:40 UTC (initiated by jen).
maya: Landed and canary started at 20:40 UTC. Watching logs and error rate.
jen: Small error blip at 20:43 (~1m) correlating with new route traffic. Metrics returned to baseline at 20:44. Holding for full 15m watch.
jen: Canary completed at 20:55 UTC with no sustained regressions. Gradual rollout to 25% started.
maya: Thanks all. We'll still open a follow-up to tighten the route validation and make the assert less flaky. Action items: 1) Andre to address the assert and add a unit test 2) Jen to add canary-level tracing for routing decisions 3) Maya to rebase any follow-ups and monitor the post-rollout dashboard. Appreciate the quick reviews :heart:
